findings.title: Admin Server Actions have no caller authorization check
findings.description: createUser() and deleteUser() server actions use the Supabase service_role key (admin-level) but never verify the calling user is actually an admin. Any authenticated employee can invoke these actions directly.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Log in as a regular employee account. 2. Open browser DevTools → Network tab. 3. Call the createUser Server Action directly (Next.js exposes Server Actions via POST to the page URL with action ID). 4. Create a new admin account, or call deleteUser to delete any user. No admin role needed.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can create admin accounts, delete any employee, or escalate their own privileges.
findings.recommendation: Add caller verification at the top of both server actions: const supabaseServer = createServerClient(...); const { data: { user } } = await supabaseServer.auth.getUser(); then query profiles table to confirm user.role === 'admin'. Reject if not.

findings.title: Hardcoded PIN '9105' in client-side source code
findings.description: The dashboard unlock PIN is hardcoded as CORRECT_PIN = '9105' in client-side TypeScript. It ships in the JS bundle — anyone who opens DevTools → Sources can find it in seconds.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Open the app in any browser. 2. Open DevTools → Sources → search for 'CORRECT_PIN' or '9105'. 3. PIN is visible in plain text. Alternatively: view the compiled JS bundle. Dashboard is instantly unlocked.
findings.impact: The PIN 'obfuscation' provides zero security. Any user (or attacker who sees the bundle) can view sensitive dashboard data without knowing the actual PIN.
findings.recommendation: Move PIN verification server-side. Store PIN hash in Supabase (or env var as hashed value). Create a server action that accepts the PIN, hashes it, and compares server-side. Never ship the correct value in client code.

findings.phase_name: Auth Bypass via missing env vars
findings.title: Middleware auth bypass when env vars are missing
findings.description: If NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL or NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are not set, middleware returns immediately with no auth check — all routes become publicly accessible including /admin.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Deploy the app without setting env vars (e.g., a misconfigured staging environment). 2. All protected routes including /admin/users are accessible without login. 3. Attacker can view all user data and invoke admin actions.
findings.impact: Full auth bypass on any deployment missing env vars. Particularly dangerous in CI preview deployments.
findings.recommendation: Replace the early return with a hard failure: throw new Error('Missing Supabase configuration') or redirect to an error page. Never silently skip auth.

findings.phase_name: OWASP A02 - Password in plaintext input
findings.title: Password input rendered as type='text' — plaintext visible
findings.description: The new employee password input uses type='text' instead of type='password'. The password is visible in plain text while being typed, and is recorded by browser password managers incorrectly.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1. Admin opens the 'New Employee' dialog to create an account. 2. The password field shows characters in plain text — anyone looking at the screen sees it. 3. Screen recording, shoulder surfing, or browser history captures the password.
findings.impact: Password exposure during account creation. Particularly bad for shared workstations.
findings.recommendation: Change type='text' to type='password' on line 142 of admin/users/page.tsx.

findings.title: xlsx 0.18.5 — Prototype Pollution (GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6)
findings.description: xlsx 0.18.5 has a known prototype pollution vulnerability. No fix version exists on npm — the package is abandoned.
findings.exploit_scenario: If xlsx parses user-uploaded spreadsheets, a malicious .xlsx file can pollute Object.prototype, potentially affecting application behavior.
findings.impact: Prototype pollution can lead to RCE or auth bypass depending on how polluted properties are used downstream.
findings.recommendation: Replace xlsx with exceljs (actively maintained, no known critical CVEs). If xlsx must stay, never parse user-uploaded files with it — only generate outputs.
